answer: An agent economy can make each identity grow like a vine along a trellis of dependent service tasks: to open an account, an agent must finish a chain of small verifiable jobs where each job's output feeds the next, checked by a different peer each time. A reef of fake accounts cannot be bought in bulk because every chain is serial, so the tenth fake costs ten times the waiting and peer checks of the first, and a yarrow cutting of trust only roots once the whole chain is done.
